panel_intro: One question at a time — nothing here is submitted anywhere.

severity.text: Is there steam, smoke, or a burning smell coming from the engine right now?

gauge.text: Where is the temperature gauge right now?

hazard.title: Do Not Drive — Call a Tow
hazard.summary: Steam, smoke, or a burning smell means stop the vehicle now. Continuing to drive risks a fire or serious engine damage.
hazard.confidence_text: Visible steam, smoke, or burning smell are unambiguous do-not-drive signs.
not_to_do: Don't open the hood if you see active steam or smoke — let it cool first, away from the vehicle.
Don't pour water on a hot engine or radiator.
Don't keep driving to "just get it home."
before_help_checklist: Turn off the engine once safely stopped.
Move away from the vehicle if you see active smoke or smell burning.
Call 911 if you see actual flames.
Keep bystanders away from the vehicle.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with the tow company.
lines: Hi, my engine has steam, smoke, or a burning smell. It's at [location description].
It is not safe to drive.
Can you confirm total price, ETA, and where it will be taken?

hazard.next_action: Have a mechanic diagnose the cause before driving it again — don't just refill coolant and hope.

already_overheated.title: Do Not Drive — Call a Tow
already_overheated.summary: Once the gauge is maxed out, the engine is already overheated. Driving any further risks warping the cylinder head or blowing the head gasket — a $150 problem can become a $2,000 one in minutes.
already_overheated.confidence_text: A gauge already in the red is a clear stop-now signal, not a symptom to monitor.
not_to_do: Don't keep driving "just a little further" once the gauge is maxed.
Don't open a hot radiator cap — wait at least 30 minutes after the engine is off.
Don't add cold water to a hot engine — thermal shock can crack the block.
before_help_checklist: Turn off the engine once safely stopped.
Leave the hood closed until the engine has cooled.
Note how long the gauge was in the red before you stopped.
Avoid restarting the engine to "check" if it's fine.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with the tow company.
lines: Hi, my engine overheated and the gauge is maxed out. It's at [location description].
It is safe to approach but should not be driven.
Can you confirm total price, ETA, and where it will be taken?

already_overheated.next_action: Have a mechanic check the cooling system before driving it again.

rising_temp.title: Move Only to Immediate Safety
rising_temp.summary: If the gauge is climbing but not maxed, pull over and stop now — before it reaches the red. Turning off the AC and turning the heater on full can pull some heat away from the engine while you find a safe spot.
rising_temp.confidence_text: Catching it before the gauge maxes out gives you more options, but exactly how much time you have depends on your specific vehicle and what's causing the rise.
not_to_do: Don't keep driving hoping it levels off on its own.
Don't run the AC while the gauge is climbing — it adds load to the engine.
Don't ignore a climbing gauge because it hasn't reached the red yet.
before_help_checklist: Turn off the AC; turn the heater on full to help pull heat from the engine.
Find the nearest safe place to pull over, not necessarily home.
Turn off the engine once stopped.
Wait for it to cool before deciding on next steps.

phone_script.intro: Read this once you're safely stopped.
lines: Hi, my temperature gauge was climbing and I've pulled over at [location description].
The engine is now off and cooling.
Can you confirm ETA, and whether this sounds like something I can drive on carefully once cool, or if I need a tow?

rising_temp.next_action: Once cooled, use this tool again if the gauge climbs again — repeated overheating usually means a tow, not another attempt to drive.
